items.sg-mgf-agentic::part-1-introduction: Singapore's Model AI Governance Framework for Agentic AI opens by defining agentic AI: software systems of one or more AI agents that plan, decide and act over multiple steps toward a user-defined goal, typically built on generative models. It names the core components - model, planning and reasoning, instructions, tools and memory, plus the safety and reliability controls and logging added in version 1.5 - and maps where the risks arise, including the systemic and multi-agent risks introduced in v1.5.
items.sg-mgf-agentic::part-2-dimension-1-asses: Dimension 1 of Singapore's voluntary framework for agentic AI asks organisations to assess and bound risks before deploying agents: determine suitable use cases, then bound risk through design by defining each agent's limits and permissions. The framework ties an agent's risk to the scope of its actions, their reversibility and its autonomy level, with system complexity and use of third-party components as additional factors in version 1.5.
items.sg-mgf-agentic::part-2-dimension-2-human: Dimension 2 makes humans meaningfully accountable across the agentic AI value chain: responsibilities are allocated clearly within and outside the organisation - version 1.5 separates platform providers from system providers and app developers - and systems are designed for real human oversight, with significant checkpoints where a person approves high-stakes or irreversible actions and practices such as monitoring human-override rates to guard against automation bias.
items.sg-mgf-agentic::part-2-dimension-3-techn: Dimension 3 covers technical controls and processes across the agent lifecycle: controls during design and development of agentic components - structural, rule-based and prompt-layer controls, distinguished in version 1.5; pre-deployment testing for baseline safety and reliability, including execution accuracy, policy adherence and tool use; and gradual rollout with continuous monitoring and testing during and after deployment, with change management sized so small changes cannot have outsized effects.
items.sg-mgf-agentic::part-2-dimension-4-end-u: Dimension 4 places part of trustworthy deployment with end users: they should be informed of an agent's range of actions, the data it can access and their own responsibilities; users who integrate agents into work processes need layered training, which version 1.5 extends with guidance on loss of tradecraft and the business-continuity effects of over-relying on agents.
